Enigma is a highly vulnerable device that relies on a series of common configuration errors. The point of entry is the exposure of sensitive credentials through sharing.

Weak. Finally, CRM access is compromised, resulting in the leakage of unauthenticated Roundcube application administrative credentials. This leads to an email account on NFS.

Gaining root privileges by injecting commands into a misconfigured internal process automation tool that operates with root privileges.

## 4. Exploitation of OpenSTAManager (CVE-2025-69212)

Navigating to http://support\_001.enigma.htb reveals the OpenSTAManager CRM application. We log in using the credentials discovered in Sandra's email (admin:Ne3s4rTars78s ).

Vulnerability Identification: This

specific version of OpenSTAManager is vulnerable to OS Command Injection during the processing of signed .p7m files (CVE-2025-69212). When a user uploads a file to verify its signature, the application calls exec() against an OpenSSL binary using the filename provided by theuser.

Exploit Strategy: We

craft a malicious .zip archive containing a .p7m file with a specially crafted filename. The filename is designed to break out of the shell command context and execute arbitrary Os commands.

We use the following Python script to generate the malicious payload ( exploit.py ):

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

We run the script and upload exploit.zip viathe "Importazione FE" (Import XML) feature in the web application. While the application displays an XML parsing error, the command injection is executed successfully in the background.

We confirm the web shell presence by issuing a test command:

curl "http://support\_001.enigma.htb/files/SHELL.php?c=id" # Output: uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)

curl "http://support\_001.enigma.htb/files/SHELL.php?c=id"
